findings: Graph accessibility/ranking is now separated from proof satisfaction: only explicit proof_eligible edges may satisfy affordance requirements; high-weight untrusted edges can activate candidates but cannot mint proof.
The adversarial high-weight untrusted-edge test preserves the correct candidate and leaves the wrong candidate incomplete.

U11 coherent semantic-access generations stage, verify, then atomically publish one generation head so readers see old or new access projection, never a mixed generation; failed/empty generations cannot replace last-known-good.
counterhypotheses: Proof-eligible labeling itself may be wrong or stale and needs provenance/authority validation.
Atomic generation publication may add rebuild/write overhead large enough to erase read-path gains.
Synthetic adversarial tests may not cover correlated graph corruption or mixed-epoch failure modes.
next_gate: Real-snapshot/Ubuntu tests for proof-eligibility provenance, mixed-generation crash/recovery, atomic publish/rollback, stale/corrupt graph and latency/rebuild cost before U11/default-read-path promotion.
ancestry_policy: These U10/U11/preprocessor changes are one coordinated development lineage and are not independent scientific replications.
